concepts.def: Electromagnetic radiation emitted by every object because of its temperature. All bodies, no matter what temperature they are, both emit and absorb infrared radiation - a block of ice, a person and a hot oven are all emitting it at the same time as they absorb it from their surroundings.

concepts.term: Emission and absorption by all bodies
concepts.def: Emitting radiation means giving it out; absorbing radiation means taking it in. These happen together and continuously: an object does not have to be hot to emit, and it does not stop absorbing while it emits. What changes from object to object is the rate at which each happens.

concepts.term: Effect of temperature on the rate of emission
concepts.def: The hotter the body, the more infrared radiation it radiates in a given time. Two identical objects at different temperatures both emit, but the hotter one emits more radiation every second.

An object that absorbs all of the radiation incident on it. A black body does not reflect or transmit any radiation. It is an idealised object - a model - not simply an object whose surface happens to look black.

Radiation arriving at a surface can bounce off it (reflect), pass through it (transmit) or be taken in by it (absorb). A perfect black body does none of the first two, so all of the incident radiation is absorbed.

concepts.term: A good absorber is a good emitter
concepts.def: A surface that absorbs radiation well also emits it well. Since a perfect black body absorbs all of the radiation incident on it, it is the best possible absorber, and therefore a perfect black body would be the best possible emitter.

How much radiation a body emits - loosely, the energy radiated per second from each square metre of its surface. Intensity is one of the two things about an emission that depend on the temperature of the body.

A body does not emit at one single wavelength. It emits over a range of wavelengths, with more intensity at some wavelengths than at others, and this spread is called the wavelength distribution. It is usually shown as a graph of intensity against wavelength.

The intensity and wavelength distribution of any emission depends on the temperature of the body. As a body gets hotter, the intensity increases at every wavelength and the peak of the distribution moves to shorter wavelengths - which is why a heated metal bar first feels warm, then glows dull red, then glows orange and finally white.

Any object in a room - a book, a wall, a person - is emitting radiation and absorbing radiation from everything around it at the same time. Explaining an everyday observation starts from that fact rather than from the idea that only hot objects radiate.

A body at constant temperature is absorbing radiation at the same rate as it is emitting radiation. Both processes are still happening; the two rates are simply equal, so the temperature does not change.

The temperature of a body increases when the body absorbs radiation faster than it emits radiation. If instead it emits faster than it absorbs, its temperature falls. It is the difference between the two rates that decides the direction of the change.

Some of the radiation arriving at the Earth is reflected straight back into space by clouds, by ice and snow and by other light surfaces. Radiation that is reflected is not absorbed, so it does not raise the temperature of the surface it bounced off.

concepts.term: Factors determining the temperature of the Earth
concepts.def: The temperature of the Earth depends on many factors including: the rates of absorption and emission of radiation, and reflection of radiation into space. The Earth's temperature settles where the total rate of absorption equals the total rate of emission back into space.

The same balance explains everyday cooling and warming. A hot drink emits faster than it absorbs, so it cools until the two rates match at room temperature; a car parked in sunshine absorbs faster than it emits, so it warms until the rising rate of emission catches up.

A typical diagram shows radiation from the hot Sun arriving mainly at short wavelengths; some is reflected back into space; the rest is absorbed by the surface and the atmosphere. The much cooler Earth then emits at longer infrared wavelengths, and gases in the atmosphere absorb some of this and re-emit it, part of it back towards the surface. Reading the arrows lets you compare the rates of absorption and emission.

options: Only objects hot enough to glow red, orange or white
All objects, whatever their temperature happens to be
Only objects that are warmer than the air around them
Only objects with a dull, dark or matt black surface
mcqs.explain: All bodies (objects), no matter what temperature, emit and absorb infrared radiation.

mcqs.q: Two identical metal blocks sit in the same room. Block X is at 80 °C and block Y is at 20 °C. Which statement is correct?
options: Only X radiates infrared, because Y is not hot at all
X radiates more infrared each second than Y does
Y radiates nothing but absorbs the infrared from X
Both blocks radiate infrared at exactly the same rate
mcqs.explain: The hotter the body, the more infrared radiation it radiates in a given time.

mcqs.q: What is a perfect black body?
options: An object whose surface is matt black rather than shiny
An object that absorbs radiation and never emits any of it
An object that absorbs all of the radiation incident on it
An object that reflects no radiation but transmits it all
mcqs.explain: This is the specification's definition; it reflects and transmits none of it.

mcqs.q: Why would a perfect black body be the best possible emitter of radiation?
options: It stores all the radiation it takes in and keeps it inside
Its black surface reflects radiation better than a shiny one
It transmits radiation straight through itself very quickly
A good absorber of radiation is also a good emitter of it
mcqs.explain: Absorption and emission depend on the same surface property, so the best absorber is the best emitter.

mcqs.q: A book has been lying on a shelf in a cool room for several hours. Which statement about the book is correct?
options: It is emitting infrared radiation and absorbing it as well
It is absorbing infrared radiation but is too cool to emit
It emits radiation only when it is warmer than the room
It emits visible light that is far too dim for us to see
mcqs.explain: All bodies emit radiation, and the book absorbs radiation from its surroundings at the same time.

mcqs.q: What does the emission from a body depend on?
options: Its temperature, which sets the intensity but not the wavelengths
Its temperature, which sets the wavelengths but not the intensity
Its temperature, which sets both the intensity and the wavelengths
Its colour, which sets both the intensity and the wavelengths
mcqs.explain: The intensity and wavelength distribution of any emission depends on the temperature of the body.

mcqs.q: A graph shows how the intensity of the radiation emitted by a body varies with wavelength, at 3000 K and again at 4000 K. Compared with the 3000 K curve, the 4000 K curve is:
options: the same height overall, with its peak at a shorter wavelength
higher at every wavelength, with its peak at a shorter wavelength
higher at every wavelength, with its peak at the same wavelength
lower at every wavelength, with its peak at a longer wavelength
mcqs.explain: Raising the temperature lifts the whole curve and moves the peak towards shorter wavelengths.

mcqs.q: A central heating radiator is switched off and cools until it is at room temperature. Which statement is then correct?
options: It has stopped emitting radiation because it is not hot now
It still emits radiation, but less each second than before
It now only absorbs the radiation coming from the warm air
It emits radiation only while its temperature is changing
mcqs.explain: Emission never stops; the lower temperature simply means a lower rate of emission.

mcqs.q: A body stays at a constant temperature. What must be true?
options: It absorbs radiation at the same rate as it emits radiation
It has completely stopped absorbing and emitting radiation
It emits radiation at a faster rate than it absorbs it
It absorbs no radiation, so its temperature cannot rise
mcqs.explain: Constant temperature is a balance between the two rates, which both continue.

mcqs.q: The temperature of a body is rising. Which statement describes what is happening?
options: It is emitting radiation faster than it is absorbing radiation
It is absorbing radiation and is not emitting any radiation
It is absorbing radiation faster than it is emitting radiation
It is absorbing and emitting radiation at exactly equal rates
mcqs.explain: The temperature of a body increases when it absorbs radiation faster than it emits it.

mcqs.q: Snow-covered ground reflects far more of the Sun's radiation than bare dark soil does. What is the effect of this?
options: The reflected radiation warms the ground as it leaves
The ground absorbs the reflected radiation a moment later
The ground emits faster to make up for the reflection
Less radiation is absorbed, so the ground stays colder
mcqs.explain: Only absorbed radiation transfers energy to the ground; reflection into space removes it.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the factors that determine the temperature of the Earth is correct?
options: It depends on the rates of absorption and emission, and on reflection
It depends only on how much radiation reaches the Earth from the Sun
It depends only on how much radiation the atmosphere can trap in
It depends only on how far the Earth is from the Sun at the time
mcqs.explain: The specification names the rates of absorption and emission of radiation and reflection of radiation into space.

mcqs.q: A cup of tea is left in a room and slowly cools down. Using ideas about radiation, which statement is correct?
options: It absorbs radiation faster than it emits it, and so it cools
It stops absorbing any radiation as soon as it begins to cool
It absorbs radiation, so its temperature must be increasing
It emits radiation faster than it absorbs it, so it cools
mcqs.explain: Emitting faster than absorbing lowers the temperature; both processes continue throughout.

mcqs.q: A greenhouse warms up through the morning and then stays at a steady temperature all afternoon. Which statement about the afternoon is correct?
options: It absorbs and emits radiation at equal rates, so it stays steady
It has stopped absorbing and emitting radiation, so it stays steady
It cannot absorb any more radiation once it has stopped warming
It absorbed radiation all morning and only emits it in the afternoon
mcqs.explain: A body at constant temperature absorbs radiation at the same rate as it emits radiation.

mcqs.q: A diagram shows radiation arriving at the Earth from the Sun and radiation leaving the Earth's surface. Which statement comparing them is correct?
options: The Earth sends back the same wavelengths that arrived at it
The Earth emits shorter wavelengths because its surface is solid
The Earth emits nothing, as the atmosphere holds the radiation in
The Earth is much cooler, so it emits at longer wavelengths
mcqs.explain: The wavelength distribution depends on temperature, and the Earth is far cooler than the Sun.

mcqs.q: On a diagram of the Earth's energy balance, the surface is shown absorbing radiation at 168 W/m² and emitting radiation at 168 W/m². What does this tell you?
options: The surface has stopped absorbing and emitting radiation now
The surface is warming, because it is absorbing radiation
The surface temperature stays constant while both continue
The surface is cooling, because radiation escapes to space
mcqs.explain: Equal rates of absorption and emission mean the temperature does not change.
